h1: Lub d Bangkok Silom — the budget Silom hostel that punches well above its price
intro: If you want a bed in the middle of Silom without paying hotel prices — and you'd like a bar, a cinema and a social scene thrown in — Lub d Bangkok Silom is the hostel solo travellers and backpackers have been coming back to since it opened in 2008. It sits on quiet Decho Road in Bang Rak, four floors of industrial-cool concrete and plywood, 36 rooms and 98 beds. Dorms from approx. THB 550/night, private rooms from approx. THB 1,400/night. About an 8-minute walk to BTS Surasak, close to the Silom night market and Patpong. The best-value bed in this area for the traveller who puts location and atmosphere first.

In-house cinema at Lub d Bangkok Silom with bean-bag chairs and free popcorn served daily

body.html: Lub d Bangkok Silom has been open since 2008 and remains one of the most-reviewed and most-booked hostels in the city — because it doesn't try to be just a cheap bed. The four-storey building on Decho Road uses industrial concrete, plywood doors and a glass-roofed stairwell that floods the common areas with natural light. The overall impression is of a place that looks sharper than anything else at this price in Silom.

Dorms come in mixed and ladies-only configurations of six to eight beds. Every bunk has its own reading light, a universal power socket and a locker beneath the mattress. Shared bathrooms on each floor are clean, with lockable cubicles. Private options include a Railway Twin (two bunk levels, shared bathroom) and a Private Double with an en-suite bathroom and a flat-screen TV. One honest note from the reviews: the dorm beds have no privacy curtains between them — if curtains matter to you, look elsewhere.

"Staff really do go above and beyond — I arrived early and they sorted breakfast for me before hours. Social areas are great for meeting people, the cinema has free popcorn every day. Incredible value for Silom."

The real draw is how much communal space the hostel packs in. There's a bar with a daily happy hour (beer from THB 50–80), an in-house cinema with bean-bag chairs and free popcorn, a lobby with seating and computer terminals, and a small terrace with yellow tables that fills up come evening. Staff run organised social events most nights — a bar crawl on Fridays, beer pong on Saturdays, snacks and get-togethers in between. If you're travelling alone and want to meet people, this hostel makes it effortless.

Location is the other reason to choose Lub d Silom. You're on a quiet sidestreet off Silom Road, about a 8-minute walk to BTS Surasak and 12 minutes to BTS Saphan Taksin, which connects you quickly to Siam, Asok or Chinatown. Street food and affordable Thai restaurants surround the block, the Silom night market (Soi 4–6) is a short walk, and Patpong is close too. Free luggage storage for up to two months makes this an ideal base if you're hopping between destinations and need to leave a bag. A score of 8.7 from over 1,200 reviews is a reliable signal that most guests leave satisfied.

The honest downsides: there is no lift, so four flights of stairs with a large rolling suitcase is genuinely hard work. Wi-Fi gets mixed reports — several reviews note it's slow or drops, especially on the upper floors. Dorm noise from late-returning guests is an occasional issue. Breakfast is not included; it's available separately for THB 90. This is not a place to hole up and work remotely — it's a place to use as a springboard for exploring Bangkok.

Tips drawn from the reviews: book ahead during the high season (December–January) and on long weekends — dorms fill fast, especially the Ladies floor. If you're a light sleeper but want to stay here, upgrade to the Private Double with en suite; the extra outlay versus sharing a dorm is modest. Don't miss the cinema during happy hour — by most accounts it's the best hour of the hostel experience.

honestSummary: Lub d Bangkok Silom is the best-value flagship hostel in the Silom area — stylish design, clean rooms, genuinely good staff, a great location and real communal amenities (bar, cinema, events). Accept that there is no lift, no curtains on dorm beds, and Wi-Fi is patchy — this is a hostel built for social travellers who spend their days out, not remote workers who need quiet and connectivity.
honestChecks: If you have heavy rolling luggage and can't manage stairs — there is no lift here and four floors of steps with a large suitcase is hard work → consider ibis Styles Bangkok Silom nearby, which has a lift and starts from THB 1,500.
If you are a light sleeper who needs silence — dorms have no privacy curtains and late-returning guests are a reality → upgrade to the Private Double en suite, or choose a hotel rather than a hostel.

If you need reliable Wi-Fi for remote work — multiple reviews flag slow or dropping Wi-Fi → bring your own SIM as a backup, or choose accommodation that specifically advertises co-working connectivity.

tips.title: Don't miss the cinema during happy hour
tips.body: The bean-bag cinema has free popcorn every day, and beer at the bar from THB 50 during happy hour — the easiest place in the hostel to start a conversation with a fellow traveller.

tips.title: Pack as light as you can
tips.body: There is no lift — four flights of stairs await. A large rolling suitcase is hard work; staff will help but it's better to pack lighter. A backpack is ideal.

tips.title: Light sleeper? Bring earplugs or upgrade to Private
tips.body: Dorm beds have no curtains and late-night noise is a reality in any lively hostel. Pack earplugs, or pay a little more for the Private Double with en suite for a quieter night.

tips.title: Book ahead in high season
tips.body: December–January and Thai public holidays see dorms fill up fast, especially the Ladies floor. Book at least two to three weeks in advance to get your preferred room type.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Lub d Bangkok Silom

faq.q: Where is Lub d Bangkok Silom and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's at 4 Decho Road, Suriyawong, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500. About an 8-minute walk to BTS Surasak and 12 minutes to BTS Saphan Taksin. Close to the Silom night market, Patpong and Lumphini Park. About 45 minutes by car or taxi from Suvarnabhumi Airport.

faq.q: What are the prices and room types at Lub d Bangkok Silom?
faq.a: Mixed dorms start from approx. THB 550/night per bed. A Ladies-only dorm bed runs around THB 650. The Railway Twin private room (bunk bed, shared bathroom) is around THB 1,400 and a Private Double with en suite starts from around THB 1,800. Prices vary by season — compare platforms before booking.

faq.q: What facilities does Lub d Bangkok Silom have?
faq.a: A bar with daily happy hour (beer from THB 50), an in-house cinema with free popcorn, communal seating areas and computer terminals, a laundry service, and free luggage storage for up to two months. Breakfast is available separately for THB 90. There is no pool, no gym and no lift.

faq.q: Does Lub d Bangkok Silom have a lift?
faq.a: No — there is no lift. The building has four floors and stairs only. If you have a large, heavy rolling suitcase this will be challenging. Staff can help, but it's worth packing as light as possible. If a lift is essential, consider ibis Styles Bangkok Silom nearby.

faq.q: Who is Lub d Bangkok Silom best suited for?
faq.a: It's ideal for solo travellers, backpackers and anyone who wants to meet people and make the most of a central Silom location on a budget. It's not the right pick for those who need privacy, silence at night, a lift, or reliable fast Wi-Fi for remote work.

faq.q: Are the dorms at Lub d Bangkok Silom safe?
faq.a: Safety is solid for a hostel. Every bunk has a personal locker beneath the mattress. The ladies-only floor is key-card-access for female guests only. Lockers are also available in public areas. The standard advice applies: keep valuables locked away rather than left on your bunk.
